q: When prices of all commodities increase, what happens to the purchasing power of money?
explanation: A general rise in prices is inflation, which decreases the purchasing power of money, so the same money buys fewer goods.

notes.text: - During inflation prices **increase**; when all prices rise, the purchasing power of money **decreases**.

q: An essential attribute of inflation is:
explanation: The essential attribute of inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level; falling production or a black market may accompany it but do not define it.

notes.text: - **Inflation**: a sustained **rise in the general price level** and a **fall in the purchasing power (value) of money**; the essential attribute is **increase in prices**.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
q: During a period of inflation prices should
explanation: Inflation is a rise in the general price level, so prices increase.

notes.text: - During inflation prices **increase**; when all prices rise, the purchasing power of money **decreases**.

q: According to RBI, which one of the following is the biggest concern of the country?
explanation: The RBI's monetary policy statements single out inflation as the main concern; price stability is the primary objective of monetary policy.

notes.text: - **RBI's biggest concern** in its policy statements: **inflation**.

q:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid in connection with inflation?

I. Cost-push inflation cycle of milk is becoming more and more pronounced in India.

II. The Bharat Atta initiative of the Government has played a considerable role in containing wheat inflation in India.

III. Retail Inflation has considerably increased in the beginning of 2024 owing to increasing commodity prices.

IV. The Bharat Dal initiative has also been extended to include moong dal.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
explanation: Bharat Atta helped contain wheat prices (II) and Bharat Dal was extended to moong dal (IV); retail inflation eased, not rose, in early 2024 (III wrong). (APPSC key: II and IV.)

notes.text: - **Bharat Atta** (subsidised wheat flour) helped contain **wheat inflation**; **Bharat Dal** (chana dal, July 2023) was extended to **moong dal**; sold via NAFED, NCCF, Kendriya Bhandar (APPSC G1 2024: II and IV).

q: To control inflation
options: it may be sufficient to use monetary policy
fiscal policy measures would alone be sufficient
A combination of monetary, fiscal and exchange rate policies may be required
key_text: A combination of monetary, fiscal and exchange rate policies may be required
explanation: Inflation control may need monetary, fiscal and exchange-rate policies together with supply management; monetary policy alone cannot fix supply-side inflation.

notes.text: - Control needs a **combination of monetary, fiscal and exchange-rate policies** – monetary policy alone cannot fix supply-side inflation; controlling inflation is **not** the Government's job only – the **RBI** has the key role.

q: Who among the following can benefit from deflation?
explanation: Deflation raises the purchasing power of money, so fixed-income groups like pensioners gain most; debtors lose because their real debt grows. Salary earners gain only if pay is not cut, so 'pensioners' is the better answer and 'all' is wrong.

notes.text: - Purchasing power of money **rises** → **fixed-income groups (pensioners, salary earners)** and **creditors gain**; **debtors lose** (heavier real debt).

q: Many a time inflation benefits
explanation: Inflation lets debtors repay loans in money of lower real value, so they gain; pensioners and consumers lose.

notes.text: - Rule: **inflation benefits debtors**; it does **not** benefit bond-holders, consumers or fixed-income groups.

q: Inflation would have most adverse effects on which of the following?
explanation: Creditors are hurt most: loans come back in money of lower purchasing power, while debtors gain.

q: Inflation, that does take into account commodities that have volatile prices, is known as
explanation:
APPSC key: core inflation. Strictly, as printed ('does take into account' volatile commodities) the stem describes headline inflation (NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC 10 p.16).
Inflation that leaves out commodities with volatile prices is core inflation (the stem means 'does not take into account').

notes.text: - Inflation that leaves out commodities with volatile prices = **core inflation**.

q: While calculating inflation, if prices of commodities which are volatile are not taken into consideration, such inflation is known as
explanation: Core inflation leaves out volatile items such as food and fuel, whereas headline inflation includes them.

notes.text: - Inflation that leaves out commodities with volatile prices = **core inflation**.

q: Who among the following is associated with the calculation of index numbers ?
explanation: Irving Fisher is the economist most associated with index numbers – his 'ideal index' (geometric mean of Laspeyres and Paasche) and the tests of index numbers; Edgeworth, Pigou and Dalton are not.

notes.text: - **Irving Fisher** is the economist most associated with **index numbers** (ideal index, tests of index numbers).

q: Out of the following which contributes the minimum amount to the Government's tax revenue?
explanation: Wealth tax was a 'paper tax' that yielded very little and was abolished in 2015; customs, income and service taxes gave far more.

notes.text: - **"Paper taxes"**: wealth, gift and estate duty – never yielded much revenue; **wealth tax** gives the **least** revenue of the major taxes.

q: Which of the following statements is true?
options: As on 2013-14, Direct taxes accounted for less than half of the total tax revenue of the Central Government
Of all the taxes levied by the centre, corporate tax is the most important one in terms of revenue generation
Income tax has played a crucial and positive role in income redistribution in rural India
GST is not related to income
key_text: GST is not related to income
explanation:
Official key: GST is not related to income. Strictly, the statement that corporate tax was the Centre's biggest tax was also true when the paper was set (corporation tax led from 2006-07 to about 2019-20).
GST is a tax on consumption (supply), not on income, so it is the intended true statement; direct taxes were well over half of Central tax revenue in 2013-14, and income tax has played little redistributive role in rural India.

notes.text: - **GST** – a comprehensive **indirect** tax on supply, **destination-based**; it is not related to income.

q: Companies Pay Corporation Tax on their:
explanation: Corporation tax is a tax on the income (net profit) of companies.

q: Excise duty is levied on which of the following?
explanation: Excise duty is levied on the manufacture (production) of goods and paid by the manufacturer; imports and exports bear customs, sales bear sales tax/VAT.

q: Which of the following is / are a direct tax?
explanation: Income tax, corporate tax and wealth tax are all direct taxes.

notes.text: - **Income, corporate and wealth taxes – all direct**; "1 and 2 only" for income + corporate tax against service tax and customs.

q: Assume that an ad valorem tax is imposed on a commodity. The price of that commodity will rise if its elasticity of demand is
explanation: With zero elasticity of demand the buyers keep buying the same quantity, so the price rises by the full tax; with infinite elasticity the price cannot rise.

notes.text: - **Incidence and elasticity**: if demand is **perfectly inelastic (elasticity zero)** the price rises by the full tax and the **consumer bears it all**; with infinite elasticity the price cannot rise.

q: Which of the following is NOT a source of their own income for the state of Andhra Pradesh?
explanation: Customs duty is a Union tax; RTO (motor vehicle) tax, electricity duty and entertainment tax are State own revenues.

notes.text: - **Not a State / AP own-revenue source**: **customs duty**, corporation tax ("taxes on companies").

q: The proceeds of the tax that are shared between the Central and State Governments in a Federal State is
explanation:
Most books and keys: income tax. Strictly, since the 80th Amendment (2000) corporation tax and customs are shared too.
Income tax (on non-agricultural income) is the classic tax levied by the Union and shared with the States on Finance Commission advice; expenditure tax was a residuary Union tax.

notes.text: - **Tax on income other than agricultural income** – the classic tax **levied and collected by the Union but distributed** between Union and States.

q: The total proceeds of the tax that accrue to the Central Government is
explanation:
Most books and keys: corporation tax. Strictly, since the 80th Amendment (2000) corporation tax is shared with the States, so no option now accrues wholly to the Centre.
Under the pre-2000 scheme corporation tax accrued wholly to the Centre; income tax and excise were shared, and estate duty proceeds went to the States.

notes.text: - **Corporation tax** is **imposed by the Central Government**; before 2000 its proceeds were **not shared** with States (Art. 270 then covered only income tax; Union excise under Art. 272) – the basis of old keys "not shared" / "accrues wholly to the Centre". **Since the 80th Amendment it is in the divisible pool.**

q: The maximum limit placed by the Constitution on levy per annum of Profession Tax is
explanation: Article 276(2) caps profession tax at ₹2,500 per person per year.

q: The maximum limit placed by the Constitution on levy per annum of Profession Tax is
explanation: Article 276(2) caps profession tax at ₹2,500 per person per year.

q: The maximum limit placed by the Constitution on levy per annum of Profession Tax is
explanation: Article 276 caps the profession tax, a State levy, at ₹2,500 a year.

q: Income tax on salary is collected and paid directly into the account of:
explanation: Income tax deducted from salaries (TDS) is a Union tax, so it is paid into the account of the Central Government, not the State, CAG or Accountant General.

notes.text: - **Income tax on salary (TDS)** is collected and paid into the account of the **Central Government**.

q: Which is not the main source of state revenue?
explanation: Taxes on companies (corporation tax) are a Union tax; land revenue, vehicle taxes and State excise on liquor and drugs are State revenues.

notes.text: - **Not a State / AP own-revenue source**: **customs duty**, corporation tax ("taxes on companies").

q: In the Union Budget 2017-18, the farmers who gave their land for the development of Capital City of Andhra Pradesh were exempted from which of the following tax?
explanation: Union Budget 2017-18 exempted farmers who gave land under land pooling for Amaravati, AP's capital, from capital gains tax.

notes.text: - Union Budget 2017-18: farmers who gave land for **Amaravati** (AP capital) under land pooling – exempted from **capital gains tax**.

q: Which of the following is the most important source of revenue for the states in India?
explanation:
sales tax/VAT was subsumed in GST on 1 July 2017 — now SGST is the States' largest own-tax source (AP 38%, 2024-25 RE) (old app notes 3:94 sub 6)
Sales tax was the States' biggest revenue source (now SGST, e.g. 38% of AP's own tax revenue, 2024-25).

notes.text: - **Most important source of State revenue**: **sales tax** (pre-2017) – now **SGST**.

exam: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
q: Which State government has announced its decision to impose Fat Tax on junk food items?
explanation: Kerala imposed a 14.5% 'fat tax' on burgers, pizzas and other junk food in its 2016 budget, the first State to do so.

q: The first State to opt for the VAT regime was
explanation: Haryana was the first State to adopt VAT, from 1 April 2003, while Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Chandigarh deferred it; the other States switched in April 2005 or later.

q: The system of VAT is applicable to
explanation: VAT in India began on commodity taxes – MODVAT (1986) and CENVAT on Union excise duties, then State VAT replacing sales tax; it never applied to income tax, estate duty or agricultural income tax.

notes.text: - VAT applies to **commodity taxes – excise duties** (MODVAT/CENVAT) and sales tax; not to income tax, estate duty or agricultural income tax.

q: Value-Added Tax is a
explanation: VAT is a multi-point tax, collected at every stage of value addition.

notes.text: - **VAT** = tax on the **value added at each stage** between production and final sale – a **multi-point**, **destination-based**, **non-cascading** tax on final consumption, borne by the consumer; invoice-credit trail makes it **self-enforcing**; a **harmonised** commodity tax that **improves revenue buoyancy** ("will diminish revenue buoyancy" is **not** VAT's idea).

q: The rate of VAT for medicines
explanation: Under State VAT, drugs and medicines were in the 4% slab.

notes.text: - **VAT rate for medicines/drugs**: the **4%** slab (pre-GST State VAT).

q: 'CENVAT' is associated with
explanation: CENVAT, which replaced MODVAT from 1 April 2000, is the credit scheme of Union excise – an indirect tax.

q: The Standing Committee of State Finance Ministers recommended in January, 2000 uniform rates across the State in respect of
explanation: In January 2000 the Standing Committee of State Finance Ministers recommended uniform floor rates of sales tax across the States.

notes.text: - **Uniform sales tax**: in **January 2000** the Standing Committee of State Finance Ministers recommended **uniform floor rates of sales tax**, implemented from **1 January 2000**.

q: Out of the options below, the most important disadvantage of a multiple tax rate structure is
options: Difficulty in remembering rates for different items
Cross subsidization amongst the taxes on different items
Difficulty in arriving at a tax rate for an item
explanation: With many rates, goods and services get misclassified into lower slabs, causing disputes and evasion – the chief drawback.

notes.text: - **Multiple tax rates** – chief drawback: **misclassification** of goods and services (disputes, evasion).

q: Which of the following descriptions does not explain VAT as per its conceptualisation?
options: It is a harmonised commodity taxation regime
It is a self-enforcing system name of
explanation: VAT is harmonised, non-cascading and self-enforcing, and it raises revenue buoyancy rather than diminishing it.

notes.text: - **VAT** = tax on the **value added at each stage** between production and final sale – a **multi-point**, **destination-based**, **non-cascading** tax on final consumption, borne by the consumer; invoice-credit trail makes it **self-enforcing**; a **harmonised** commodity tax that **improves revenue buoyancy** ("will diminish revenue buoyancy" is **not** VAT's idea).

q: Implementation of uniform sales tax in India commenced from 1st January
explanation: Uniform floor rates of sales tax were implemented by the States from 1 January 2000.

q: Which state is collecting VAT through E-payment?
explanation: The key gives Karnataka, an early leader in e-payment of VAT/commercial taxes.

notes.text: - **Karnataka** – early e-payment of VAT/commercial taxes; **Maharashtra** – the State the **IMF** had advised earlier not to adopt VAT (APPSC key).

q: Which of the following states was advised earlier by the IMF not to adopt VAT system?
explanation: The APPSC key gives Maharashtra as the State the IMF had earlier advised not to adopt VAT.

notes.text: - **Karnataka** – early e-payment of VAT/commercial taxes; **Maharashtra** – the State the **IMF** had advised earlier not to adopt VAT (APPSC key).

q: Small dealers, whose annual turnover does not exceed ..., should be exempt from the liability of VAT.
explanation: The VAT design of 2003 exempted small dealers with annual turnover up to Rs 10 lakh (printed key; later the 2005 White Paper used Rs 5 lakh, with States free up to Rs 10 lakh). (Moved to the tax-system row.)

q: Which of the following taxes is the largest source of revenue for the Government of India?
explanation:
corporation tax overtook excise in 2006-07 and income tax leads since about 2020 — now income tax is the largest Central tax (21% of the rupee, BE 2026-27) (Union Budget 2026-27 at a Glance p.6, p.10)
When this was asked (2003) Union excise duties were the largest Central tax (₹91,433 crore in 2002-03 against corporation tax ₹48,616 crore) (now income tax).

notes.text: - **Union excise** was the largest Central tax until **2005-06**; **corporation tax** led from **2006-07** to about 2019-20; **income tax** since then.

q: The Govt. of India gets maximum revenue from
explanation:
corporation tax overtook excise in 2006-07; now income tax is the largest Central tax (BE 2026-27) (Union Budget 2026-27 at a Glance p.6, p.10)
In 2005-06, the year before this paper, Union excise was the Centre's biggest tax (₹1,12,000 crore RE against corporation tax ₹1,03,573 crore) (now income tax).

q: Among the tax revenues of the Union Government, the most important source is
explanation:
excise was overtaken by corporation tax in 2006-07 — now income tax is the largest Central tax (BE 2026-27) (Union Budget 2026-27 at a Glance p.6, p.10)
In 2003-04 (the year of this paper) Union excise was the Centre's most important tax (BE ₹96,791 crore against corporation tax ₹51,499 crore) (now income tax).

notes.text: - **Union excise** was the largest Central tax until **2005-06**; **corporation tax** led from **2006-07** to about 2019-20; **income tax** since then.

q: By how much percentage the direct taxes, collected by the Income Tax department for Telangana and Andhra Pradesh have gone up in the 2022-23 financial year compared to the previous year?
explanation: The APPSC key gives 8.5% growth in direct taxes collected by the Income Tax department for AP and Telangana in 2022-23; the exact regional figure could not be verified.

notes.text: - Direct taxes collected by the IT department in **AP and Telangana** rose about **8.5%** in 2022-23 (APPSC 2023 key).

exam: APPSC 2018 Special Qualifying Test for Appointment by Promot
q: During the first four decades of planning in India, principal component of revenue of the central government was from
explanation: In the first four decades of planning the Centre's main revenue came from indirect taxes (excise, customs); direct taxes overtook them only in 2007-08.

notes.text: - **First four decades of planning**: main Central revenue from **indirect taxes**; developing countries still get more from indirect taxes.

q: The biggest taxation source of the Government of India is
explanation:
now personal income tax is the biggest Central tax (BE 2026-27) (Union Budget 2026-27 at a Glance p.6, p.10)
In 2007-08 corporate income tax (RE ₹1,86,125 crore) was the Centre's biggest tax, ahead of excise and personal income tax (now personal income tax).

q: Which of the following is the largest contributor to the total tax revenue of India?
explanation:
now income tax is the largest Central tax (BE 2026-27) (Union Budget 2026-27 at a Glance p.6, p.10)
In 2002-03, the year of this paper, Union excise duties (₹91,433 crore) were the largest Central tax, well ahead of corporation tax (₹48,616 crore); corporation tax led only from 2006-07.

q: How can expanding the tax base contribute to increased government revenue without changing tax rates?
options: By lowering the exemption threshold to include more taxpayers
By providing more tax exemptions and deductions
By focusing exclusively on corporate tax collection
key_text: By lowering the exemption threshold to include more taxpayers
explanation: Widening the tax base, e.g. by lowering the exemption threshold, brings more taxpayers in and raises revenue at unchanged rates; more exemptions shrink the base, and tariffs or corporate-only focus are not base-widening.

notes.text: - **Widening the tax base** (lower exemption threshold, fewer exemptions) raises revenue without changing rates – the **Chelliah approach: lower rates, broader base**.

q: A tax that takes higher proportion of income from those with low incomes than from those with high incomes is called
explanation: A regressive tax takes a higher share of income from the poor than from the rich; a progressive tax does the opposite.

q: Laffer effect implies
options: Reduction in the rate of taxation leads to more than proportionate increase in tax yield
Reduction in the rate of taxation leads to less than proportionate increase in tax yield
Reduction in the rate of taxation leads to a proportionate increase in tax yield
Reduction in the rate of taxation leads to no change in the tax yield
key_text: Reduction in the rate of taxation leads to more than proportionate increase in tax yield
explanation: The Laffer effect: a cut in tax rates leads to a more than proportionate increase in tax yield.

notes.text: - **Laffer effect**: **reduction in tax rates leads to a more than proportionate increase in tax yield**; Laffer curve – **inverted U**, zero revenue at 0% and 100%; **Arthur Laffer** (1974); term coined by **Jude Wanniski**.

q:
Consider the following
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R) and choose the correct code:
Assertion (A): Tax reforms directed towards a simple tax system will result in positive productivity gains.
Reason (R): They boost GDP growth and employment growth by removing deadweight costs and reduce distortions in resource allocation.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
key_text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A).
explanation: Both are true and R explains A: a simpler tax system raises productivity by removing deadweight costs and resource-allocation distortions.

notes.text: - **Simpler tax system** → **productivity gains** by removing **deadweight costs** and resource-allocation distortions (APPSC G1 2024: A and R true, R explains A).

q: The Kelkar Committee is related to:
explanation: The Kelkar Task Forces (2002) gave two reports, on direct and on indirect taxes.

q: The Chairman of the Committee that recommended Agricultural Holding tax in India is
explanation: The K.N. Raj Committee (1972) on agricultural wealth and income taxation recommended an agricultural holding tax.

q: The amount of tax to be paid is proportionate to the value of the commodity in respect of
explanation: An ad valorem tax is a percentage of the value of a commodity; a specific tax is a fixed amount per unit.

notes.text: - **Ad valorem tax** = **% of the value** of a commodity; **specific tax** = fixed amount per unit (weight/quantity).

exam: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
q: Which of the following is the pecuniary burden imposed on individuals or property owners by the legislative authority to support the government?
explanation: A tax is a compulsory pecuniary burden imposed by the legislature to support government, with no quid pro quo; a fee pays for a specific service, and cess and surcharge are particular kinds of tax.

q: Which of the following is not a tax?
explanation: MAT (Minimum Alternate Tax), GST and VAT are taxes; SAT is the Securities Appellate Tribunal, not a tax.

notes.text: - **SAT** (Securities Appellate Tribunal) is **not a tax**; **MAT** (Minimum Alternate Tax, 1996-97), GST and VAT are.

q: As per India’s Economic Survey 2021-22, as a percent of GDP, what was the gross tax revenue of the Central Government in 2019-20?
explanation: The Economic Survey 2021-22 put the Centre's gross tax revenue at 9.9% of GDP in 2019-20.

q: Chelliah Committee (1992-93) recommended that in Income Tax there should be
options: Broader spread between minimum and maximum rates
explanation: The Chelliah Tax Reforms Committee (1991-93) asked for lower rates, fewer slabs, a broader base and minimum incentives/exemptions – not higher rates or wider spreads.

q: Which Committee recommended Tax on agricultural holdings?
explanation: The K.N. Raj Committee (1972) recommended a tax on agricultural holdings; Bhoothalingam, Wanchoo and Chelliah did not. (Printed: no key.)

notes.text: - Agricultural holding tax / agricultural wealth and income → **K.N. Raj** (not Chelliah, not Wanchoo = black money, not Bhoothalingam = rationalisation of wages/incomes, not Kaldor).

q: Tax on agricultural holdings was recommended by
explanation: The K.N. Raj Committee (1972) on taxation of agricultural wealth and income recommended the Agricultural Holding Tax; Wanchoo dealt with black money and Chelliah with general tax reform.

notes.text: - Agricultural holding tax / agricultural wealth and income → **K.N. Raj** (not Chelliah, not Wanchoo = black money, not Bhoothalingam = rationalisation of wages/incomes, not Kaldor).

q: Which one of the following was constituted to deal with taxation of agricultural wealth and income in India?
explanation: The K.N. Raj Committee, 1972 dealt with taxation of agricultural wealth and income; Kaldor (1956) covered expenditure, wealth, gift and capital gains taxes and Wanchoo (1971) black money.

q: Kelkar committee is associated with
explanation: Vijay Kelkar's task forces (2002) gave recommendations on tax reforms (direct and indirect taxes).

q: In 2012-13 year for senior citizens in the age group of 60-80 years, the income tax exemption limit
explanation: Budget 2012-13 set the exemption limit at ₹2.5 lakh for senior citizens (60-80), ₹2 lakh for others and ₹5 lakh for very senior citizens.

q: Of the various criteria that make filing of income tax returns mandatory, which was removed in the 2002-2003 budget?
options: Membership of any club with payment of a specified fee
explanation: Under the one-by-six scheme, filing was compulsory for anyone showing one of six lifestyle signs; Budget 2002-03 dropped the telephone connection criterion, while club membership and other signs stayed.

notes.text: - **One-by-six scheme**: return filing compulsory for anyone showing any one of six lifestyle signs; the **telephone connection** criterion was dropped in Budget **2002-03**.

q: Which of the following has been removed as one of the criteria for mandatory filing of income tax returns in the budget for 2002-2003?
options: Membership of a club with a certain amount of membership fee
explanation: Budget 2002-03 dropped ownership of a telephone connection from the one-by-six criteria for compulsory return filing; foreign travel, club membership and other signs remained.

notes.text: - **One-by-six scheme**: return filing compulsory for anyone showing any one of six lifestyle signs; the **telephone connection** criterion was dropped in Budget **2002-03**.

explanation:

q: As per Budget 2020, which of the following is incorrect about the income tax rates?
options: For the income range rupees 0 to 2.5 lakh is the tax rate
For the income range rupees 2.5 to 5 lakh is the tax rate 5
For the income range rupees 5 to 7.5 lakh is the tax rate 10
For the income range rupees 2.5 to 10 lakh is the tax rate 20
key_text: For the income range rupees 2.5 to 10 lakh is the tax rate 20
explanation: Budget 2020's new regime had nil up to ₹2.5 lakh, 5% for 2.5-5 lakh and 10% for 5-7.5 lakh; there was no single 20% band for ₹2.5-10 lakh, so that statement is the incorrect one.

q: Exemption of income tax for individuals is available on interest paid in respect to which loan?
explanation:
Most books and keys: Housing. Strictly: interest on an education loan is also fully deductible under Section 80E (since AY 2006-07), so 'Educational' is equally correct (general knowledge, not checked).
Interest on a housing loan is deductible (Sec 24(b)) – the answer books and keys give; automobile loan interest is not.

notes.text: - **Deductions**: interest on a **housing loan** (Sec 24(b)) is deductible; interest on an **education loan** is also deductible (**Sec 80E**); **Section 80C** covers NSC (and its accrued interest), PPF, EPF, life insurance, tuition fees of **two** children, home-loan **principal**.

q: Which of the following get tax rebate under the 80 C Act?
options: The school fees of three children in one family
Tax rebate of 20% in Employments Provident Fund
Interest earned on National Saving Certificate
key_text: Interest earned on National Saving Certificate
explanation:
Most books and keys: interest on NSC. Strictly: the principal part of home-loan EMIs also qualifies under 80C, so 'Home Loans EMIs' is partly right (general knowledge, not checked).
Accrued interest on National Savings Certificates is deemed reinvested and qualifies under Section 80C; tuition fees count for only two children, and EPF has no '20% rebate'.

notes.text: - **Deductions**: interest on a **housing loan** (Sec 24(b)) is deductible; interest on an **education loan** is also deductible (**Sec 80E**); **Section 80C** covers NSC (and its accrued interest), PPF, EPF, life insurance, tuition fees of **two** children, home-loan **principal**.

explanation: MAT is imposed on the book profit of zero-tax companies that otherwise pay little or no corporate tax; it is not a tax on films, capital gains or professionals.

q: The Minimum Alternative Tax (MAT) was introduced in the budget of the Government of India for the year
explanation:
Most books and keys (NextGen, UPSC 1997): 1996-97. Strictly: MAT was first introduced by the Finance Act 1987 (Budget 1987-88, Sec 115J, AY 1988-89), withdrawn in 1990 and reintroduced in 1996-97 (NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC 02 p.22).
Among the options, MAT came in the Budget of 1996-97 (Sec 115JA), which is the year books and keys give; its first version of 1987 had been withdrawn in 1990.
